description: Seaducks are primarily found foraging in waters less than 20 meters deep.
context_quote: Figure 8.39 in § 8.4.4(F)(1) of this Part illustrates the areas within the Ocean SAMP boundary with water depths less than 20 m (66 feet) and therefore is thought to represent the primary foraging habitat for the thousands of seaducks that winter in the Ocean SAMP waters.

description: Common eiders forage in water less than 10 meters deep during winter.
context_quote: Common eiders forage in water less than 10 m (33 feet) during the winter when diving over rocky substrate and kelp beds.

description: Scoters typically forage in waters less than 20 meters deep, especially during winter.
context_quote: Maximum diving depths of scoters are about 25 m (82 feet), although most birds probably forage in water less than 20 meters (66 feet) deep, particularly during the winter months.

description: Seaducks may be found in waters up to 25 meters deep, but foraging behavior is uncertain.
context_quote: Paton et al. (2010) did detect seaducks in waters up to 25 meters (82 feet) deep during aerial surveys, although it was unclear from the aerial surveys if the seaducks were foraging or engaging in other behaviors such as roosting.

description: Common eiders are 100% found in waters less than 16 meters deep.
Black scoters are 100% found in waters less than 20 meters deep.
